title: Celestial Bodies
author: Dimitris Yfantidis
summary: Thousands of textured spheres drawn with instanced OpenGL.
description: Thousands of textured spheres scattered through a spherical shell around the origin, drawn in instanced batches with OpenGL 3.3 and lit by a point light at the centre. This is the scene the N-body simulation will set in motion.
how_it_works: One sphere mesh (32 x 64 segments, about 4,000 triangles) is uploaded to the GPU once. All 3,318 spheres are drawn from it with instanced rendering: each glDrawElementsInstanced call draws up to 500 copies, and the vertex shader moves and scales every copy using its instance number to look up a position and a radius.
Lighting is diffuse (Lambert) shading from a point light at the origin plus a little ambient light, applied to a texture of a fictional Ceres-like surface.
The bodies sit at random directions and distances (20 to 400 units) from the origin; the camera orbits that point in spherical coordinates.
highlights: Thousands of spheres from just seven draw calls per frame.
The sides facing the centre are lit; the far sides fall back to the ambient light.
Zoom out with numpad minus to see the whole shell of bodies.
